questions.q: Why do duplicate customer records still occur even with a shared party registry?
options: Because reps may skip searching first, or two business units may enter the same customer independently
Oracle Fusion does not allow searching for existing parties
Because every business unit is required to create its own separate party
Because merges happen automatically and create duplicates
questions.explain: Duplicates typically arise from skipped searches, independent entry across business units, or a rename that creates a new party instead of updating the old one.

questions.q: What happens to a duplicate account's open and historical transactions when it is merged?
options: They are deleted permanently
They move to the surviving account, so aging and statements reflect the true combined balance
They remain stuck on the duplicate account forever
They are automatically written off
questions.explain: Merging consolidates transaction history onto the designated surviving account rather than leaving it split across two records.

questions.q: What happens to the duplicate account itself after a merge?
options: It is permanently deleted from the system
It becomes the new surviving account
It is inactivated, preserved for audit trail, but can no longer be transacted against
It is automatically merged again into a third account
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion inactivates the duplicate rather than deleting it, keeping a record for audit purposes while preventing further transactions.

questions.q: Besides merging, which of these is an example of routine customer maintenance?
options: Automatically generating a new transaction type
Running AutoInvoice
Creating a new ledger
Inactivating an account or site that's no longer used, without merging it
questions.explain: Inactivating unused accounts or sites, updating profile/credit data, and correcting addresses and contacts are all routine maintenance separate from merging.

questions.q: In the Cascade Outdoor Supply merge example, how was the surviving account chosen?
options: The one with more existing transaction history was designated as the survivor
Randomly, by the system
Whichever account had the lower account number
The account created most recently
questions.explain: The AR team deliberately designated the record with more transaction history as the surviving account before merging the duplicate into it.
